audit.whatIsWrong: Four separate strings build the level-6 plan around "Abyssal Voyage" (content spikes[2].text, wants.you[2], wants.foe[2], mid, whys[4]).
audit.why: Tahm Kench has no Abyssal Voyage. champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json: W = Abyssal Dive (dive + knockup, 1000/1050/1100/1150/1200 range, 21/20/19/18/17s), R = Devour. Abyssal Voyage was the pre-rework global ultimate. The entry tells the player their level-6 answer to Chaaaaaaaarge!!! is an ability that does not exist, which means they have no answer at all.
audit.corrected: Level 6 gives Devour, not a global. The correct level-6 plan is to hold Devour for a dismounted Kled so he cannot rebuild courage.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — W Abyssal Dive, R Devour

audit.whatIsWrong: content `early` says "once his W (Jousting double-dash) and mounted Q are both up".
audit.why: Jousting is Kled's E, not his W. His W is Violent Tendencies (four-attack attack-speed steroid, autoReset). The entry gets this right in spikes[1] and wrong in early, so a reader tracking "his W" watches the wrong ability.
audit.corrected: Jousting is E (13/12/11/10/9s, 550 range, recastable to dash back through the initial target). Violent Tendencies is W (13/12/11/10/9s).
sources: champ-data/_kits/kled.json — slot E Jousting, slot W Violent Tendencies

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3], whys[3] and `late` all sell the "3-stack stun into Devour combo"; full tradeGood and dosFull repeat it.
audit.why: Tongue Lash at 3 stacks "stuns and the stacks are consumed", and Devour requires three stacks to fire on an enemy champion. The stun destroys the resource the ultimate needs. Against Kled specifically this is a losing line twice over: you spend your stacks on a 1-2s stun instead of the multi-second removal that stops him rebuilding Skaarl's courage.
audit.corrected: Build to three stacks, then spend them on Devour. The Q stun is the fallback when Devour is on cooldown or he is already mounted and healthy.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — An Acquired Taste, Tongue Lash

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere explains that a dismounted Kled gains courage by hitting you, or that Pocket Pistol is what his Q becomes.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Kled can restore Skaarl's courage by fighting enemies. At maximum courage, Kled remounts with a portion of Skaarl's health." and Q "When dismounted, this ability is replaced by Pocket Pistol, a ranged gun blast that knocks back Kled and restores courage." So the standard Tahm Kench instinct — brawl the dismounted Kled with your huge HP pool — is exactly what refills him. This is the single decisive mechanic of the matchup and the entry never mentions it.
audit.corrected: A dismounted Kled must land damage to remount. Devour him (he cannot hit anything from inside you), or disengage entirely. Do not stand in Pocket Pistol range trading autos while his courage bar fills.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kled.json — Skaarl, the Cowardly Lizard; Bear Trap on a Rope / Pocket Pistol

audit.whatIsWrong: The cooldown block says "track Beartrap on a Rope" with no numbers, and never mentions that the Jousting recast — not the first dash — is his escape.
audit.why: Bear Trap on a Rope is 11/10/9/8/7s; Jousting is 13/12/11/10/9s and "Kled can cast this ability again to dash back through his initial target". Punishing after the first dash walks into a free return dash. The window is after the recast. Also: the trap's yank is delayed — "If shackled for a short duration, the target takes additional physical damage and is yanked toward Kled" — so the hook landing is the cue to move, not the pull.
audit.corrected: Bear Trap on a Rope 11s at rank 1 down to 7s. Jousting 13s at rank 1 with a recast return — commit only after he has spent the recast. The trap yanks on a delay, so react when it lands.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kled.json — Bear Trap on a Rope, Jousting cooldowns and descriptions

audit.whatIsWrong: The displacement race is never framed, despite both champions carrying knockups.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags it: Abyssal Dive (W) vs Bear Trap on a Rope (Q), whoever lands it first owns the trade. The cooldowns make that one-sided — his displacement is 11s at rank 1, yours is 21s. You cannot win this on cooldown parity; you have to bait the trap out first.
audit.corrected: Your Abyssal Dive is 21s, his trap is 11s — roughly two of his to one of yours. Never open with Abyssal Dive; make him throw the trap, then dive.

audit.whatIsWrong: No burst tell is given for Violent Tendencies.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags the auto-reset. Violent Tendencies grants massive attack speed for four attacks and "the fourth attack deals more damage". The readable tell is the buff going up, and the correct reaction is to leave before the fourth attack, not after it.
audit.corrected: When Violent Tendencies lights up, count his attacks — disengage before the fourth, which is the one that hurts.

audit.whatIsWrong: diff is "EVEN" and diffRating "6/10" on a 45.81% matchup, and the level chart hands Tahm Kench 4 of 7 stages while content `mid` says the opposite in prose.
audit.why: 45.81% over 334 games is a losing lane, not an even one — it is the second-worst entry in Tahm Kench's whole top-lane table (only Heimerdinger at 43.96% is lower, and that one is correctly labelled TRICKY 7.5/10). The internal contradiction is concrete: content `mid` opens "Levels 4 and 5 are genuinely his" while win[3] says "Tahm Kench" and full phases[3].side says "Skill". Three different answers for the same stage.
audit.corrected: TRICKY / 7.5-8/10, and Levels 4-5 belong to Kled in both layers — rank-3 Bear Trap is 9s and Violent Tendencies is up for every trade while Abyssal Dive is still 21s and Devour is not online.
sources: packet tahmkench.json — winRate 45.81, games 334; champ-data/tahmkench.full.js diff table (heimerdinger 43.96 = TRICKY 7.5/10)

audit.whatIsWrong: full breakdown/itemization prescribes "Add anti-heal (Thornmail component early) — his healing fights your grind."
audit.why: Kled is not flagged for needs-antiheal in _missing-interactions.json, and nothing in his kit text is healing in the Grievous Wounds sense — the remount restores Skaarl's health from a courage bar filled by dealing damage. Whether Grievous Wounds interacts with the remount is not answerable from the kit file, and I did not verify it, so I am not proposing an edit; flagging it as unverified rather than asserting either way.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kled.json — Skaarl, the Cowardly Lizard; champ-data/_kits/_missing-interactions.json (no needs-antiheal row for kled)

edits.before: Abyssal Voyage lets you side-step Kled's R engage entirely or punish him teleporting elsewhere while you hold the side lane with Thick Skin.
edits.after: Devour is your level-6 answer to a dismounted Kled — swallow him so Pocket Pistol and free autos cannot rebuild Skaarl's courage for the remount.

edits.before: Use Abyssal Voyage to reposition or escape when Kled pops his R charge and your Flash is down
edits.after: Save Devour for a dismounted Kled — every hit he lands rebuilds courage toward a free remount

edits.before: Run his R charge at you when your Flash and Abyssal Voyage are both on cooldown
edits.after: Run his R charge at you when your Flash and Abyssal Dive are both on cooldown

edits.before: Kled's Chaaaaarge!!! R gives him a guaranteed engage path and your Abyssal Voyage is your only clean answer — if both are down he dictates the fight.
edits.after: Chaaaaaaaarge!!! is 140s at rank 1 and reaches 3500 — your clean answer is Devour on a dismounted Kled, which stops him rebuilding courage entirely.

edits.before: Level 1 you have the edge — Tongue Lash's range lets you slow Kled repeatedly off the minion wave before he can close for his Q grab, and Thick Skin starts banking grey health from any chip he lands. The danger is levels 2 and 3: once his W (Jousting double-dash) and mounted Q are both up, Kled can brawl through your passive healing and chunk you badly before you hit 3 An Acquired Taste stacks. Don't trade extended early — fish one Tongue Lash slow, let him burn his dash, back off, and heal the grey health before you commit to a second exchange. Never let him land the Q grab when Skaarl's courage is full; that's his kill setup, not yours.
edits.after: Level 1 you have the edge — Tongue Lash reaches 900 against Bear Trap on a Rope's 800 and Jousting's 550, so you slow him off the wave for free, and Thick Skin banks any chip he lands. The danger is levels 2 and 3: once Jousting (E, 13s) and Violent Tendencies (W) are both up, Kled brawls through your passive healing and chunks you badly before you hit 3 An Acquired Taste stacks. Don't trade extended early — fish one Tongue Lash slow, then wait out the Jousting recast rather than the first dash, because the recast is the escape. Never let him land the trap when Skaarl's courage is full; that's his kill setup, not yours.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are genuinely his — Kled's mounted combo deals more short-trade damage than your stun into Devour can net you before he bounces out with Jousting. Play for CS and stack fishing rather than all-ins, and always track Skaarl's courage bar: a dismounted Kled is helpless, so if he takes you to near-even HP in a trade and pops off, press him hard before remount triggers. Level 6 shifts things back your way: Abyssal Voyage means his R charge no longer has a guaranteed landing — you can pool away or simply not be there, and the global repositioning threat lets you influence the map rather than face his chaos 1v1 in a straight brawl.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are genuinely his — Kled's mounted combo out-damages anything you net before he bounces out on the Jousting recast, and his trap is 9s at rank 3 while Abyssal Dive is still 21s. Play for CS and stack fishing rather than all-ins, and always track Skaarl's courage bar: a dismounted Kled is helpless, so if he pops off in a trade, press him hard before remount triggers — but never trade autos with him there, because every hit he lands refills courage. Level 6 is your real shift: Devour on a dismounted Kled removes him for the duration, and he cannot hit anything back into courage from inside you.

edits.before: With all 3 An Acquired Taste stacks reliably online you can stun-into-Devour his all-in attempts, and if he dismounts you win the remount race by pressing him under tower.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are his: rank-3 Bear Trap on a Rope is 9s and Violent Tendencies covers every trade, while Abyssal Dive is still 21s and Devour is not online yet.

edits.before: Heartsteel or Sunfire Aegis lets your grey-health healing absorb Kled's mounted trades and your 3-stack stun into Devour combo becomes a genuine kill threat.
edits.after: Heartsteel or Sunfire Aegis lets your grey-health healing absorb Kled's mounted trades, and 3 stacks spent on Devour — not on the Q stun — is a real kill threat.

edits.before: First item Heartsteel or Sunfire Aegis is your true lane stabiliser — grey-health healing absorbs most of what Kled does in a mounted skirmish, and the stun-into-Devour combo at 3 stacks either removes him from a team fight entirely or burns his Flash. At 2+ items you are near-unkillable in prolonged skirmishes, but Kled's R is a team-fight nuke and his remount passive lets him survive your Devour window and come back angry — respect the R engage range, keep Tongue Lash as a peel tool off your carries rather than engaging solo, and let your team's follow-up do the actual killing.
edits.after: First item Heartsteel or Sunfire Aegis is your true lane stabiliser — grey-health healing absorbs most of what Kled does in a mounted skirmish, and Devour at 3 stacks either removes him from a team fight entirely or burns his Flash. The Q stun consumes those same stacks, so never open with it. At 2+ items you are near-unkillable in prolonged skirmishes, but Kled's R is a team-fight nuke and his remount lets him survive your Devour window and come back angry — respect 3500-plus of R range, keep Tongue Lash as peel off your carries, and let your team finish.

edits.after: Devour him dismounted, don't spend the stacks stunning. Tahm Kench wins the Bear Trap on a Rope windows.

notes: Four edits here are enum-style fields, not prose: content win[3], full phases[3].side, full diff and full diffRating. They cannot satisfy the +/-10% length band by construction ("Skill" -> "Kled", "EVEN" -> "TRICKY"), so if the applier bands every string these four will be discarded and will need applying by hand. They are the fix for a concrete internal contradiction: content `mid` says "Levels 4 and 5 are genuinely his", content win[3] says Tahm Kench, and full phases[3].side says Skill — three answers for one stage. Separately: full itemization tells you to buy anti-heal against Kled ("his healing fights your grind"). Kled is not flagged for needs-antiheal in _missing-interactions.json and nothing in his kit text is healing in the Grievous Wounds sense; I could not verify whether Grievous Wounds touches the courage remount, so I left that string alone. Worth a human check. The name in the full layer is "Beartrap on a Rope" in roughly a dozen strings; Riot's name is "Bear Trap on a Rope". I fixed the three highest-visibility ones (tldr, focus.text, breakdown.cooldowns); the rest of the full layer still carries the compressed spelling.
